Returns whether an automorphism a acts trivially on the tree. For contracting groups see also and .
gap> L := AutomatonGroup("p=(p,q)(1,2), q=(p,q)"); < p, q > gap> IsOne(q*p^-1*q*p^-1); true

Computes the order of an automorphism a. In some cases it does not stop. Works always (modulo memory restrictions) for groups generated by bounded automata.
If InfoLevel of InfoAutomGrp is greater than or equal to 3 (one can set it by SetInfoLevel( InfoAutomGrp, 3)) and the element has infinite order, then the proof of this fact is printed.
gap> L := AutomatonGroup("p=(p,q)(1,2), q=(p,q)"); < p, q > gap> Basilica := AutomatonGroup( "u=(v,1)(1,2), v=(u,1)" ); < u, v > gap> Order(p*q^-1); 2 gap> SetInfoLevel( InfoAutomGrp, 3); gap> Order( u^35*v^-12*u^2*v^-3 ); #I u^35*v^-12*u^2*v^-3 acts transitively on levels and is obtained from (u^35*v^-12*u^2*v^-3)^1 by taking sections and cyclic reductions at vertex [ ] infinity gap> SetInfoLevel( InfoAutomGrp, 0);

Operations with tree automorphisms and homomorphisms
productfor tree homomorphisms The multiplication of tree homomorphisms is defined in the standard way.
actionof tree homomorphism on letter actionof tree homomorphism on vertex The following operations allow computation of the actions of tree homomorphisms on letters and vertices.
gap> L := AutomatonGroup("p=(p,q)(1,2), q=(p,q)"); < p, q > gap> 1^p; 2 gap> [1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1]^(p*q^2); [ 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2 ]
The operations below describe how to work with sections of tree homomorphisms.
